title: Investigate client exit crash
final_messages:
Repaired both active Z archives and updated the shared writers to preserve the ordering.

All 547,108 records and 70,505 unrelated entries were preserved. The 30 focused tests passed.

No new crash report appeared after the observed client closure. You stopped Computer Use, so controlled exit testing remains unverified.

[Backups and repair report](<G:/3.3.5a - Dev/BK/client-exit-repair-20261003-092330/repair-report.json>).

Repository lint checks encountered existing C++/SQL issues.

The crash comes from **corrupted character appearance caches**, exposed when WoW frees them during exit.

The [8:53:58 crash report](<G:/3.3.5a - Dev/Errors/2026-10-03 08.53.58 Crash.txt:114>) traces through WoW’s appearance cleanup into Windows heap cleanup, which attempts to read address `0x23`.

I found the underlying defect in `CharSections.dbc`:

- Both `patch-Z.MPQ` and `patch-enUS-Z.MPQ` contain appearance groups split across separate parts of the table.
- WoW assumes those groups are contiguous. Reproducing its allocation logic identified **65 writes past allocated array bounds**.
- Reordering the same rows correctly reduced those overflow writes to **zero**, preserving every record.

That explains why simply exiting crashes: the memory damage happens earlier, when appearance data loads.

The repair is to order rows by race, sex, section type, variation, and color in both archives, and preserve that ordering in the generators. **No client files were changed; the repair still needs a live exit check.**

title: Assess Dreadlord 3.3.5 retroport
final_messages:
The repaired patch is ready and passes the new UV lookup check. Please close WoW and tell me when it’s closed so I can replace `Data\Patch-Dr.MPQ`; Windows locks that archive while the client is running.
Installed the repaired `Patch-Dr.MPQ`. My first export omitted Wrath’s UV lookup table; all 28 draw batches now pass validation. Verified backups are preserved.

Launch WoW fresh and retest:

```text
.npc add temp 8716
.npc add temp 9516
```

Please confirm whether both normal and green dreadlords are now visible.

Fully restart WoW with `Patch-Dr.MPQ` in `Data`, then use these GM commands:

- Normal Dreadlord: `.npc add temp 8716`
- Green Lord Banehollow: `.npc add temp 9516`

Both NPC entries are verified in your live database. These create temporary spawns.

For a quick preview on yourself, clear your target and run `.modify morph target 130` for normal or `.modify morph target 8609` for green. Restore your appearance with `.modify morph reset`.

Built [Patch-Dr.MPQ](G:/Downloads/HDWoWModels/Patch-Dr.MPQ) as a standalone NPC override.

Includes normal/green variants, recovered Retail textures, and all 124 animation entries with eight external animations embedded. Archive and asset checks pass.

Ready to copy into your client’s `Data` folder; **not installed yet**. Live visuals remain untested, and some Retail effects are approximated. [Port report](G:/RetroPorterWork/dreadlord/PORT.md)

**Yes—this is a strong candidate for retroporting.** I inspected the folder, reviewed all four linked chats, and ran conversion checks in memory.

| Intended result | Estimated chance of success |
|---|---:|
| Working animated NPC or morph in 3.3.5 | **85–95%** |
| Polished playable race with equipment and player actions | **60–75%** |

These are engineering estimates; in-game rendering hasn’t been tested.

The strongest evidence:

- **The supplied model is already simplified:** 31,775 vertices versus Retail’s 83,805, comfortably below Wrath’s 65,535 limit.
- **Its rig is intact:** 204 bones and 124 animation entries. Bone identities, hierarchy, pivots, and animation order match the current Retail model.
- **Conversion works structurally:** the existing converter produces native `MD20` version 264 and retains all 124 animation entries.
- **The supplied LOD skin is particularly useful:** it preserves all 45,374 triangles while splitting sections into palettes of at most 64 bones, within Esteria’s native helper limit.
- **Animation checks pass with our established reading rules:** all eight external animations convert, and 2,259 external timestamp arrays have valid ranges and ordered timestamps. The earlier timestamp warning came from reading external offsets as in-model data during inspection.

There are several concrete issues to handle:

- **Incomplete dependencies:** the folder omits 18 referenced textures and eight animation files. All eight animations and 17 textures are readable from your local Retail installation. One shockwave effect texture fails local decoding and needs recovery.
- **Body texture cleanup:** its main image decodes correctly, but trailing mip-table entries are invalid. It should be normalized before packaging.
- **Rendering differences:** Retail shaders, edge fading, and some particle behavior require Wrath-compatible approximations.
- **Playable limitations:** the model lacks authored dance, mount, and sheath sequences. Equipment, customization controls, and weapon events would require additional work.

**I recommend an isolated NPC proof first**, using the supplied split LOD skin, recovered dependencies, explicit skin-texture bindings, and the animation handling established in the previous ports. That should establish appearance, movement, combat, casting, and talking before expanding into playable-race support.

Nothing was installed or modified.
